requirements.title: Every FUNCTION or function ENTRY has a function result whose name is a class (1) local identifier
requirements.definition: For each FUNCTION statement or ENTRY statement in a function subprogram, there is a function result; that result is a variable or procedure pointer, and its name is a local identifier of class (1).

pending.function-statement-result-exists: Runtime plan defines integer function f() assigning f=47 and checks caller receives 47, distinguishing the result variable from an unrelated host sentinel.
pending.entry-statement-result-exists: Source-use plan for ENTRY in a function subprogram records the entry result object; executable ENTRY coverage remains under the procedure owner.
pending.function-result-variable-or-procedure-po: Source plan uses one ordinary variable result and one procedure-pointer RESULT case after procedure-pointer dependencies are registered; no pointer-address oracle is used.
pending.function-result-name-class-one-local: Name-resolution plan pairs a function result name with a global homonym control under 19.3.1 so the class (1) local status is load-bearing.

requirements.oracle: Source accounting only. Future executable fixtures must establish a positive nondefault state first, use sentinels distinct from every value the exercised construct can write, and observe only portable name-resolution, scope, type, value, or source-admission properties. No diagnostic is claimed for an unnumbered program restriction. Diagnostic wording, processor-created external names, addresses, storage layout, image/team execution, and compiler agreement are not oracles.
requirements.oracle_limitation: This source packet creates no Fortran fixture, compiler invocation, execution evidence, fixture approval, oracle approval, or coverage claim. Pending plans are source-derived designs or explicit source-use boundaries. Negative source controls are retained only as future optional diagnostics unless a numbered rule or another registered owner supplies a required diagnostic obligation.
